1.why: All six screens are static, flat-styled pages with no animations, carousels, banners or pop-up dialogs; only inline cards and a static log panel.

2.why: Each step has a large bold dark-blue heading and a single high-contrast teal primary button, though the dark 'Logs' panel visually competes with the actual task card.

3.why: Each page holds only one task, but the information she actually needs (the reset code and the MFA code) is hidden inside a developer-style 'Logs (training simulation)' panel with no clear signposting, and there is no progress indicator.

4.why: The flow spans six sequential steps and requires her to locate and transcribe a 40+ character random reset code from the log panel plus a 6-digit MFA code, and to hold four separate password composition rules in mind.

5.why: No password manager support, autofill hints, 'remember me' checkbox, show-password toggle or paste helper appears on any screen.

6.why: Nothing familiar or previously saved is surfaced — no remembered account identifier, no masked email/phone hint, and the codes shown are opaque random strings.

7.why: Wording is plain and sentences are short ('Enter your account identifier', 'Use at least 12 characters...'), though some helper text is small grey type at low contrast.

8.why: No error or validation state appears anywhere in the six screenshots, so no message describing a problem and its fix can be observed.

9.why: Step 1 gives a concrete example value ('use demo-account') and step 3 lists password requirements, but no sample password, no code format example, and no worked example of where to copy the code from.

10.why: The fields that exist are clearly labelled ('Reset code', 'New password', 'Six-digit verification code'), but no alternative sign-in options such as biometric/face, magic link or phone call are offered at all.

11.why: Every screen presents only one task with at most two buttons (e.g. 'Verify code' plus 'Request another code'), so choices are minimal.

12.why: The log panel appends a plain-language line after each action and step 6 gives an explicit green success summary, though intermediate steps show no dedicated confirmation banner before moving on.

13.why: Each new step carries a short explanatory tip or callout (privacy-neutral response note, 'Codes expire after 10 minutes', 'Check the visible Logs panel', password rules).

14.why: 'Request another code' on step 2 and 'Return to recovery start' on step 6 allow retries, but there is no back link, cancel option or edit path on the password, MFA or consent steps.

15.why: All six screens reuse the same header, teal rule, white rounded card, label/input styling, teal primary button, log panel and footer warning.
